docs.title: Blender 5.1 NPR Port - New Features & Usage Guide
Project Introduction
docs.text:
Blender 5.1 NPR Port is an NPR-specialized Blender fork that combines features from Goo Engine and 4.4 NPR-prototype with additional useful specialty nodes.

Most features are Eevee exclusive and do not support Cycles.

docs.title: Documentation Scope
docs.text: This documentation covers NPR/Eevee extension features that have been added to Blender 5.1 NPR Port compared to official Blender 5.1 and currently exist in this branch, as well as their basic usage methods.

docs.title: Extended Shader Nodes
docs.text: This page documents the major shader nodes added to Blender 5.1 NPR Port.

docs.title: Render Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access render target properties.

Outputs: - Frag Coord - Fragment/pixel coordinates (X, Y, Z, W) - Width - Render target width in pixels - Height - Render target height in pixels

Usage: Use in calculations that require screen resolution or pixel position.

docs.title: Scene Time Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access time-based values for animation.

Inputs: - Scale - A value used to scale frame numbers

Outputs: - Frame - Current frame number - Seconds - Elapsed time in seconds - Timeline - Timeline position mapped to 0-1 - Scaled Frame - Frame number after scaling

Usage: Create time-based animations and effects.

docs.title: Screen Derivative Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Detect edges and gradients in screen space.

Outputs: - DDX - X direction derivative - DDY - Y direction derivative - DDXY - Combined DDX + DDY

Usage: Edge detection, gradient mapping, and post-process effects.

docs.title: Portal In / Portal Out
docs.text:
Purpose: Organize node links with named portal values.

Usage: - Portal In stores a named value in the current node tree. - Portal Out retrieves that value later in the same tree.

Limits: - Works only within the same shader node tree. - Cannot cross node trees or node groups automatically.

docs.title: Render Texture Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Sample a render texture configured in scene settings.

Inputs: - Vector

Outputs: - Color - Alpha

docs.title: Screenspace Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access color and depth buffers from the current render.

Inputs: - View Position

Outputs: - Scene Color - Scene Depth

docs.title: World Environment Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Sample Eevee world environment color.

Inputs: - Direction

Outputs: - Color

docs.title: World To Tangent Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Convert a world-space direction into tangent space.

Inputs: - Vector

Outputs: - Vector

docs.title: Basis Transform Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Transform points, vectors, or normals between custom bases.

Inputs: - Vector - Origin - X Axis - Y Axis - Z Axis

Outputs: - Vector

docs.title: Bevel Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Generate an approximate beveled normal in Eevee.

Inputs: - Radius - Normal

Outputs: - Normal

docs.title: Curvature Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Provide curvature and rim outputs from screen-space data.

Inputs: - Samples - Sample Radius - Thickness - Scale

Outputs: - Scene Curvature - Scene Rim

docs.title: Shader Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Provide shading-related information such as diffuse, shadow, and ambient lighting.

Inputs: - World Position - Normal

Outputs: - Diffuse Shading - Shadow - Ambient Lighting - Half-Lambert Factor

docs.title: Light Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access per-light information.

Outputs: - Color - Power - Type - Position - Direction - Radius - Spot Size - Sun Angle

Usage: Use For Each Light for per-light workflows.

docs.title: Scene Color Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Read scene data in filter materials.

Inputs: - UV / Coordinate

Outputs: - Color - Depth - Normal

Parameters: - Source - Color / Depth / Normal / Emission / Environment

Usage: Post-process effects, reflections, depth-based effects.

docs.text:

Tip

For detailed parameters and usage, refer to Blender's official shader node documentation together with the NPR Port extensions.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Control whether material preview thumbnails are rendered in dropdown and search lists.

This is mainly used to reduce lag when opening the material selector in scenes with many materials.

docs.title: Entry Point
docs.text: Edit > Preferences > Editing > Objects > Materials > Material Selector Previews

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• When enabled, the material selector shows previews according to the current logic.

  • When disabled, the selector falls back to plain material icons and no longer triggers preview rendering in the dropdown list.

  • The default value is enabled.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• Only affects material previews inside dropdown lists such as template_ID(...).

  • Does not affect the large preview sphere in the Material Properties panel.

  • Does not affect the actual material render result.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: • Lets you choose a collection that is not affected by the world environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: NPR Tree is a flexible, node-based non-photorealistic rendering pipeline. It supports custom line rendering, toon shading, and artistic effects.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Per-light processing using For Each Light
  • Real-time preview in viewport
  • Built-in node groups for effects (shadows, toon, etc.)
  • Complete shading control

docs.title: NPR Input Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Main input for NPR Tree processing

Outputs (9 total): - Base Color - Material base color - Metallic - Metallic property - Roughness - Surface roughness - Normal - Surface normal - Alpha - Transparency - Emission - Self-emission color - IOR - Index of refraction - Light Direction - Light source direction - Specular - Specular reflection strength

docs.title: For Each Light Node
docs.text: Purpose: Process rendering for each light source in the scene

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: NPR Tree is a node tree attached after a regular material to perform color post-processing, allowing shader output to be stylized in color form.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Per-light processing using For Each Light
  • Real-time preview in viewport
  • Built-in node groups for effects (shadows, toon, etc.)
  • Complete shading control

docs.title: NPR Input Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Main input for NPR Tree processing

Outputs (9 total): - Base Color - Material base color - Metallic - Metallic property - Roughness - Surface roughness - Normal - Surface normal - Alpha - Transparency - Emission - Self-emission color - IOR - Index of refraction - Light Direction - Light source direction - Specular - Specular reflection strength

docs.title: For Each Light Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Process rendering for each light source in the scene

Outputs: - Light Index - Current light ID starting from 0 - Light Direction - Direction from surface to light source - Light Distance - Distance to light source - Light Color - Light color value - Light Energy - Light intensity

Usage Pattern: 

NPR Input → For Each Light → [Calculate per-light effects]
                                → Merge results → Output

Common Uses: - Toon shading with multiple light tones - Per-light cel shading - Multi-pass lighting effects

docs.title: Image Sample
docs.text:
• Sample textures within NPR Tree
  • Input: Image, UV coordinates
  • Output: Color, Alpha

docs.title: NPR Refraction
docs.text:
• Control refraction in the NPR pipeline
  • Parameters: IOR, Roughness

docs.title: Built-in Node Groups
docs.text:
• Cavity - Shadow-based shading
  • Kuwahara Filter - Artistic smoothing
  • Curvature Shading - Edge-based effects
  • Shading Models - Prebuilt toon/stylized shaders

docs.title: Simple Toon Shading Setup
docs.text:
1. Create a material with Principled BSDF
  2. Add an NPR Tree node
  3. In the NPR Tree (Ctrl+Tab):
  4. Connect NPR Input to For Each Light
  5. Sample lighting properties
  6. Apply toon shading from node groups
  7. Merge all light contributions
  8. Output the result to the material
  9. Render in viewport or final output

Tip: Test with different light setups for best results.

Warning

NPR Tree is Eevee-exclusive. Not available in Cycles.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text:
Render Textures is a scene-level Eevee additional render texture system.

It allows the scene to maintain up to 4 Render Texture slots, each of which can specify a camera and an output type. The scene result from that camera perspective is first rendered into a texture, then sampled in regular object materials through the Render Texture node.

docs.title: Panel Entry Point
docs.text: Scene Properties > Render Textures

docs.title: Configurable Parameters
docs.text:
Each Render Texture entry currently supports:

Parameter Description Name Identifier name of the texture entry, used for referencing in nodes Enabled Enable or disable rendering of this texture Source Choose what to capture: Color / Depth / Normal Camera Specify the camera for rendering this texture Resolution X/Y Output texture pixel dimensions Update Mode Update frequency: Every Sample / Every Frame / Manual Format Output precision: RGBA16F / RGBA32F / R16F / R32F

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Render Textures
  2. Create a new entry
  3. Select Source, Camera, resolution, and format
  4. Add a Render Texture node in object materials
  5. Select the corresponding entry in the node panel
  6. Use the node output in material calculations

Tip

Perfect for creating real-time reflections, screen-space effects, and dynamic textures.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text: It is a scene-level Eevee full-screen filter stack. Each entry is a Filter domain material that processes the current frame in list order.

docs.title: Panel Entry Point
docs.text:
Scene Properties > Filter Materials

Node tree entry point: Shader Node Editor > Shader Type > Filter

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Filter Materials
  2. Create a new entry or click New Filter Material
  3. The selected material must be a Filter domain material
  4. Open the Shader Editor and switch the top Shader Type to Filter
  5. Use Scene Color in the filter material to read scene data, then output through Filter Output
  6. Choose the execution location through Execution Stage

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• The default sampling coordinate for Scene Color is the Window output of the Texture Coordinate node

  • AOV input is supported

  • Execution stages:

    • Before Volume Fog

    • Before Depth of Field

    • Before Composite

    • The selected material must be a Filter domain material
    • Open Shader Editor and switch the top Shader Type to Filter
    • Use Scene Color to read scene data
    • Output the result with Filter Output
    • Select filter execution position via Execution Stage

docs.title: Execution Stages
docs.text:
• Before Volume Fog - Execute before volume fog processing
  • Before Depth of Field - Execute before depth of field
  • Before Composite - Execute before compositing

Note

Filter Materials can only use Filter domain materials.

Use Cases

  • Color grading and tone mapping
  • Screen-space effects (e.g., edge detection, toon rendering)
  • Motion blur and motion vector effects
  • Post-process denoising and sharpening
